extracted.intended_audience: public companies, asset managers and asset owners, preparers and users of financial disclosures, and other organizations considering supporting or implementing TCFD recommendations
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for organizations to disclose climate-related risks and opportunities through existing financial reporting, covering governance, strategy, risk management, and metrics & targets. Also describes who should support the recommendations, what support implies, and where to find implementation resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governance
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose the organization’s governance around climate-related risks and opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the TCFD core framework; see the TCFD recommendations report for expanded guidance and examples of governance disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose the actual and potential impacts of climate-related risks and opportunities on the organization’s businesses, strategy, and financial planning where such information is material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include consideration of risks and exposures over the short, medium, and long term; the 2017 TCFD recommendations report and the 2021 TCFD Annex provide implementation guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk Management
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose how the organization identifies, assesses, and manages climate-related risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain processes for identification, assessment and management of climate risks as part of existing risk-management disclosures; resources on methods are available on the TCFD Knowledge Hub.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metrics & Targets
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose the metrics and targets used to assess and manage relevant climate-related risks and opportunities where such information is material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report metrics and targets that are used internally to manage climate risks and opportunities; use the TCFD Knowledge Hub and implementing guidance to select appropriate measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who can support the TCFD recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations with public debt or equity and asset managers and owners — the preparers and users of financial disclosures — are particularly encouraged to support and implement the recommendations. Other supporters can range from industry associations, to central banks, governments, regulators and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support is broad and may include many types of organizations; being a supporter does not carry a single prescriptive set of requirements for every type of organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: What it means to be a TCFD supporter
rubrics_metrics.description: Support indicates that your organization believes the TCFD recommendations provide a useful framework to increase transparency on climate-related risks and opportunities. Supporting organizations are expected to encourage TCFD implementation. For companies, support is a commitment to work toward their own implementation of the TCFD recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different supporter types (e.g., credit rating agencies, stock exchanges, government agencies) have different but important roles to play in encouraging and implementing TCFD-aligned disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefits of better disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Better climate-related disclosure should enable: (a) Risk assessment — more effectively evaluate climate-related risks to your company, its suppliers, and competitors; (b) Capital allocation — make better-informed decisions on where and when to allocate your capital; (c) Strategic planning — better evaluate risks and exposures over the short, medium, and long term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These benefits are the rationale for adopting TCFD recommendations and may be used to explain the value of disclosure to boards, investors, and other stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to become a TCFD supporter
rubrics_metrics.description: Expressing support is as simple as completing the TCFD support form with the proper approvals from your organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no cost to become a supporter; immediate step after expressing support is being added to the public list of supporters on the TCFD website; longer-term engagement is encouraged as organizations implement recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation resources and guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Where to find tools: The TCFD Knowledge Hub (launched May 2018 with CDSB) is an online platform housing relevant insights, tools, and resources to help organizations implement the TCFD recommendations, with over 400 resources covering governance, strategy, risk management and metrics & targets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Knowledge Hub, the 2017 TCFD recommendations report, and the 2021 TCFD Implementing Guidance/Annex for practical implementation help; contributors include nonprofits, intergovernmental institutions, academics, industry associations, consultants, and corporates; additional resources are added continuously.
